title: Why crickets chirp faster on warm nights
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Do crickets chirp faster when it is hot?
Can you tell the temperature from cricket chirps?

explain.say: On a warm summer night, crickets chirp quickly. On a cool night the same crickets chirp slowly.

draw.text: Why crickets chirp faster on warm nights

explain.say: Crickets are cold-blooded: their bodies are the same temperature as the air. When it is cool, the chemistry in their muscles runs slowly, so their wings open and close more slowly.
When it is warm, their muscles work faster and the chirps speed up. The chirp rate rises in a fairly straight line as the temperature goes up.
In 1897 Amos Dolbear wrote a rule for this. For the snowy tree cricket, count chirps in 25 seconds, divide by 3 and add 4 to get roughly the temperature in degrees Celsius.

faq.q: Do crickets chirp faster when it is hot?
faq.a: Yes. Crickets are cold-blooded, so warmer air makes their muscles work faster and they chirp faster. In cool air they slow down.
asks: Why do crickets chirp slower in the cold?

faq.q: Can you tell the temperature from cricket chirps?
faq.a: Roughly, yes. For the snowy tree cricket, count chirps in 25 seconds, divide by 3 and add 4 for the temperature in degrees Celsius. It works less well for other kinds of cricket.
asks: How do I use a cricket as a thermometer?

faq.a: Dolbear's law is a rule published by physicist Amos Dolbear in 1897 linking how fast crickets chirp to the air temperature. Warmer air means more chirps per minute.
asks: What is the cricket temperature rule?

faq.a: A cold-blooded animal, like an insect, does not make much of its own body heat, so its body warms and cools with its surroundings. Its activity speeds up when warm and slows when cold.

faq.q: Do crickets stop chirping when it is cold?
faq.a: Yes. Below a certain temperature, often around 10 to 13 degrees Celsius for many species, crickets usually fall silent because their muscles are too sluggish.
asks: Why are crickets quiet in winter?
At what temperature do crickets stop?

facts: Physicist Amos Dolbear published his rule linking cricket chirp rate to temperature in 1897.
For the snowy tree cricket, the number of chirps in 25 seconds divided by 3, plus 4, gives roughly the temperature in degrees Celsius.

quiz.say: A snowy tree cricket chirps 60 times in 25 seconds. Using Dolbear's rule, about what is the temperature?
quiz.show: 60 chirps in 25 s: divide by 3, add 4. About…
quiz.why: 60 divided by 3 is 20, and adding 4 gives about 24 degrees Celsius.

wrong.1: That adds 4 to 60 without dividing by 3 first.
wrong.2: That is too cold for so many chirps; follow the rule: 60 divided by 3 is 20, plus 4.
